_comment: Records, per edge function, the SHA-256 of the local source at the moment it was
last known to match production. edge-function-drift.mjs recomputes the hash and
fails when a source changes without the deploy being recorded.
WHY THIS EXISTS. edge-functions-versioned checks that a deployed function HAS a
source file. It passed while 20 of 25 local sources differed from production,
including apex-sync, whose four fixes sat undeployed for 4h38m until a human
noticed. A guard that cannot fail on the thing it guards is decoration.
redacted:true means the local copy was RECOVERED from production with its shared
admin key replaced by a placeholder. Production is the source of record for those
and DEPLOYING THEM WOULD BREAK THEM. The hash still pins them, so a silent edit

apex-probe.note: Real source, read-only GET probe, admin-key gated. Deployed v1 on 10 Aug 2026 and recovered into the repo in 4222e85 because the source existed only in the deployment. Reads TG_ADMIN_KEY from integration_secrets at run time — no literal in the file, so this is the real source and not a redacted recovery copy. verify_jwt true.

apex-sync.note: Real source. Deployed v5 on 11 Aug 2026, and pinned at deployed_version 2 while production ran 4 - which is how the divergence hid. Production v4 held entityHasEverReturnedRows()/holdCursor and the REPO DID NOT; the repo also held the 71-line ?probe=metrc block that production did not. Neither side was a superset. Production's guard was merged into the repo FIRST (209b212), so this deploy adds the probe without deleting the zero-row cursor hold. verify_jwt TRUE, unchanged.

budz-chat.note: Real source, and now genuinely byte-deployed. Deployed v5 on 11 Aug 2026. Production had been running v4 for days: the OLD system prompt that argued grams per square foot of canopy against the owner's locked facts, Haiku with a 900-token ceiling, a 24k context slice, no seat catalogue, no report catalogue and no web search. Every one of those corrections was committed and never shipped. verify_jwt stays TRUE - the function reads the caller identity out of the verified header to bind asCaller and call tg_ai_gate; flipping it false would break its whole auth model.

parse-documents.note: Real source. Deployed v7 on 11 Aug 2026 by Agent I. TWO things in one deploy and the second was not planned. Planned: rule G2 - OURS was a hardcoded licence pair that its own comment called KNOWN DEBT deliberately not fixed; literal-licences went 57 to 59 and failed the build, so it is fixed here. It now loads from company_licenses and FAILS CLOSED with 503, because an empty list would make every manifest record US as the counterparty. UNPLANNED: THE REPO WAS BEHIND PRODUCTION. The repo held a v4/v5-era file with no identity parser and no v6 regression fix while production ran v6, and THIS GATE CANNOT SEE THAT - it compares the repo to this pin, not to production, so it said deploy it. Deploying the repo would have shipped the v5 bug that wrote NULL over client_name and client_license on five certificates, erasing the field rule C0 calls the only independent source of who grew the material. Caught by reading production first. Production v6 was merged into the repo and G2 applied on top; nothing from v6 removed. Same shape as apex-sync on 10 Aug. verify_jwt false, unchanged - the admin key is the gate.

coa-inspect.note: Real source. Deployed v1 on 10 Aug 2026 and recovered into the repo on 11 Aug 2026 by Agent I, verbatim from the deployment - it had been running for a day with no source anywhere, found by diffing the 27 live functions against the 26 with source. READ ONLY: it downloads a stored certificate and reports what the text actually extracts to, so the COA parser can be written against reality rather than an assumption. Writes nothing. Admin-key gated with a constant-time compare, key read from integration_secrets at run time, so no literal in the file. verify_jwt false, which is correct here because the admin key is the gate.

alert-email.note: Real source, WRITTEN AND NOT YET DEPLOYED - deployed_version 0 says so rather than implying a deploy that never happened. Sends the missed-sync alerts the owner asked for on 12 Aug 2026 ("I NEED TO GET AN ALERT EVERY TIME A SYNC IS MISSED"). It reads ALERT_EMAIL_API_KEY from the secret store at run time and contains no literal, and it FAILS CLOSED with a readable reason when the secret is unset - which it is, until the owner pastes a Resend key into Settings then Keys & Connections. Pinned here because an unpinned function is invisible to edge-function-drift, which is exactly how twenty sources once differed from production unnoticed. Deploy with verify_jwt=true.
